It started with a cough.
Walter White. Fifty years old. A chemistry teacher with a second job at a car wash.
Then the doctor said it. Lung cancer. Inoperable.
And a man who had swallowed his pride his whole life became Heisenberg.
But what if the cough was just a cough?
No diagnosis. So no ride-along with his brother-in-law, Hank.
He never sees his old student, Jesse Pinkman, climbing out of a window.
Jesse keeps cooking small. Probably gets caught. Probably lives.
Jane wakes up. No plane falls out of the sky over Albuquerque.
Hank never chases Heisenberg. He retires, and tells the same old stories at every barbecue.
And Walt? Walt keeps grading papers. Keeps swallowing it.
Because the cancer didn't create Heisenberg.
Gray Matter did. Walt sold his share for five thousand dollars. It became worth billions.
The pride was always there. The cancer just gave him permission.
So in this timeline, Walter White lives to be eighty.
Safe... Respected... Forgotten.
At the very end, he finally admitted it.
I did it for me... I liked it... I was good at it... And I was really... I was alive.
Without the cancer, he lives thirty more years.
He's just never alive.
